This Handcrafted Transit Camper Van Was Built by a Veteran Carpenter, It's Now for Sale
26 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / brianmcgaha
Today's featured project is based on a 2026 AWD Ford Transit 350 with a 148" wheelbase and a high roof, finished in a rare Wild Green paint.
It was created by Pinnacle Campers, a Boise, Idaho-based company specializing in custom camper vans. Brian McGaha founded the company in reaction to a growing amount of clients requesting camper van conversions and vehicle upfitting. He has been a carpenter and a residential remodeling contractor for around 30 years.
As always, let's first take a look at the van's exterior. The vehicle rides on VanCentric wheels wrapped in Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires.
The van came with a Quigley Q-Lift paired with a Bilstein strut and shock upgrade – they offer a 2-inch lift and better stability when driving both on and off the beaten path.
At the rear, you'll come across a setup I haven't seen before. There's an FVC (Flatline Van Co.) spare tire carrier/ladder combo attached to the driver-side door - that's a super common upgrade . However, the part that I haven't seen before is an A/C unit mounted to it.
Climb on top of the van, and you'll discover an AVC RIG roof rack holding a 600 W solar array and a flat-mounted Starlink antenna.
Other notable mods are Transit Trail running boards, power and water hookups, a CR Laurence window on the driver's side, and flares.
Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to fit a bed in an east to west arrangement instead of the standard north to south. This rig's Flarespace flares are paint matched to the van's color.
The rugged exterior theme shifts to a more modern, homey look inside the van. The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a large curtain to separate the two areas for more privacy.
Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice Lonseal Madera "mushroom" flooring, custom white cabinetry with a two-part epoxy finish, brown automotive tweed fabric on the walls, and a grey ceiling with 8 lights. The look is complemented by a stained walnut countertop.
The first part of the living space is a seating area located dead ahead as you enter. It comprises a large bench with a Lagun table mount and several storage compartments.
The bench also hides an unexpected feature: a shower. Specifically, if you lift one of the bench's tops, you'll reveal a stainless steel shower pan and showerhead connected to a mixer. To complete the shower setup, you must hang a curtain to hooks on the ceiling. It's a really small setup, but it will do the job whenever you don't have access to a public shower.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a stainless steel sink with a fold-down faucet and a small cover, a slide-out housing a portable single-burner 1,800 W induction cooktop (that can also be accessed from outside the van), and another slide-out holding a 45-liter Dometic CFX345 chest-style fridge.
An overhead cabinet, two drawers, and a lower cabinet are available for storage in the kitchen. Moreover, on the opposite side, you'll come across a relatively tall unit integrating a drawer and three open storage compartments.
Two of the storage compartments hold bins, and the third and largest one at the bottom has a Trelino separating toilet.
Beside the kitchen overhead cabinet, Brian devised a simple control panel for some of the rig's utilities. It has a monitor for the water tank, a thermostat, and light switches (including a main dimmer switch) and switches for the inverter, Starlink system, and water pump.
Finally, you'll discover a fixed bed arrangement in the back part of the living space. It's 75 inches (190 centimeters) long and 52 inches (132 centimeters) wide, with a 6-inch-thick (15-centimeter-thick) memory foam mattress. The bedroom also offers four overhead cabinets (two on each side) and two reading lights.
You can store your largest items in the garage underneath the bedroom, which is accessible from both inside and outside the van. Besides offering room for cargo in its middle part, the garage has two boxes on the sides that offer extra storage space and accommodate part of the utility systems.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are two 300 Ah lithium batteries and a 2,500 W inverter. Three charging sources help keep the batteries topped off: solar power, shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running thanks to two 50-amp DC-DC chargers.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 21-gallon (79-liter) freshwater tank, a heated and under-mounted 16-gallon (60-liter) greywater tank, a Seaflo pump with an accumulator, an Aqua Crest water filter, and an outdoor shower connection.
The last important system is an Elwell Timberline hydronic heater providing both heated air and hot water. On those hot days, the Nomadic Cooling S1 mounted at the back of the van can rapidly cool you off, as its internal unit sits right next to the bed.
All in all, Brian created a mobile home with the right blend of practicality, comfort, and storage space. As mentioned in the title, this Transit-based camper is now for sale.
According to Pinnacle Campers' listing , its price tag is $154,500 (€138,617). Considering the fact that it's a brand-new platform with less than 900 miles (1,448 km) and all of the comforts it offers, that's a fair price.
